To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the health ministry in a transition setting must: 1) develop a strategic plan that identifies the most important health priorities and the roles that the health ministry should play to support their achievement; 2) strengthen its ability to monitor progress and hold its staff and partners accountable; and 3) develop the capacity to work in partnership and to orchestrate the work of others.
the reorientation of the Ministry of Health in transitional Vietnam has been constrained by a lack of information systems, weak planning systems, and inadequate accountability systems.
health authorities in developing countries often must cope with rapid changes that have important implications for their roles and the leverage they can exercise throughout the health system.

reorientation of the health ministry role is a complex process that requires a comprehensive and detailed approach.
reorienting health ministry roles in transition settings is a difficult and time consuming process that requires a long-term commitment to capacity building and strategic planning.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we need to move away from a focus on the health workforce and toward a focus on the system of health services and the roles of health managers in the system.
the Ministry of Health needs to develop a new set of skills and capabilities, and to build a new institutional architecture to support them.
the Ministry of Health in Vietnam has made significant progress in strengthening its capacity to manage the health workforce, but there is still a long way to go.
The main takeaway from our work is that

health system reform in developing countries requires a more sophisticated understanding of the roles of the ministry in the overall system and a better appreciation of the challenges involved in shifting from the exercise of administrative control to strategic steering.
the health system in transition is a complex adaptive system that requires a more nuanced and sophisticated approach to health system management.

the Ministry of Health in transitional Vietnam, as elsewhere in developing countries, must reorient its approach to health workforce management to one of overall orchestration and steering, rather than one of direct control, if it is to achieve its goals.
